Monastyryska Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Monastyryska's Jewish community, present from 1625, identified strongly with Hasidism after David-Zvi Oyerbach (1743–1808) founded a dynasty in the town in the late 18th century, later managed by his son Nachman-Zeev (1790–1856). Four synagogues operated by 1910. Following the German occupation of July 1941, Jews from Koropets and surrounding villages were brought to Monastyryska in 1942, and about 1,000 people were deported to the Bełżec death camp that October; the remnants of the community were deported to Buchach, documented elsewhere in this collection. Around 20 local Jews survived the war. This is the older of two Jewish cemeteries in Monastyryska, both later replaced by public squares after 1945.
